metaDescription: Estimate a child's adult height from the parents' heights with the mid-parental method, with the usual range of 8.5 cm either side.
intro: Estimate adult height from the parents' heights.
why:
Enter the mother's and father's heights and the child's sex. The mid-parental method adds 13 cm to the sum for boys or subtracts 13 cm for girls, divides by two, and shows a range of 8.5 cm either side (about two standard deviations, per the MSD Manual).

It is a population estimate. A child's own growth pattern, nutrition and health matter more, and a doctor can judge a growth chart far better than this formula.
howTo: Read the predicted height and range.

faq.a: Most children land within the range, but some do not. It cannot predict an individual.

faq.q: Does it work for children who are not biological children of both parents?
faq.a: No. It relies on the parents' genes.
